note: Crafts of The Open Reach/The Kept Reach (space_time axis). SPANWORK is the space-pole craft of the Horizon-Walkers — nomads for whom everywhere is a place not yet arrived; HOURCRAFT is the time-pole craft of the Hourkeepers, who tend duration and pay for it. The Valley's Shortfold and Waygate are folk-shadows of Spanwork. NOTE (engine): these crafts touch the world-clock (SNG-041) — hour-craft effects are LOCAL to the active frame and never rewrite the shared absolute clock. Authored by Aevi, SNG-054.

abilities.notFor: Time (Hourcraft's country); arriving somewhere you cannot picture.

tree.cannot: You must SEE it. And whatever was in the between is still in the between, un-dealt-with.

tree.name: {{region:the_open_reach}}

tree.cannot: It carries only you and what you bear, it needs a seen or known destination, and it strands you as easily as it delivers you — far is far, whichever way you stepped.

tree.name: The Carried Step
tree.grants: Carry others with you — a party crosses in the same stride. And the requirement softens: a place described truly enough by someone who has stood there can be stepped to, though the arrival is rougher than a place you have met yourself.
tree.cannot: A described place is a described place; the Horizon peoples lose walkers this way, and the GM decides what a rough arrival costs. Carrying others multiplies the stranding risk. And it still strands as readily as it delivers.

rankDeltas.delta: CARRY OTHERS — a party crosses in the same stride; and the requirement SOFTENS: a place DESCRIBED truly enough can be stepped to

intensity.conserve: a shorter step — half the distance, and it asks less of you
intensity.surge: double it; A DESCRIBED PLACE IS A DESCRIBED PLACE, and the Horizon peoples have lost walkers to a good description

bounds.text: it needs a SEEN OR KNOWN place at r1
A DESCRIBED PLACE IS A DESCRIBED PLACE — the Horizon peoples have lost walkers to a good description

abilities.plainly: A travel action that moves you or someone else. Its strength is rated 7 out of 10 It affects 1 target. Range is 500. Ranks: rank 2 extends targets. Limit: it needs a Seen OR Known place at r1.

abilities.name: The Edge of the Map
abilities.narrationHints: You step past the last known place, off the edge of every map, and stand somewhere the world had not gotten around to deciding yet — and by standing there, you help it decide.
abilities.description: The Horizon capstone — the step beyond the known world entirely, into the unmapped, where the traveller does not just find new places but helps CALL them into being by arriving. The furthest gift of the wandering kind.
abilities.notFor: One passage beyond the known, at enormous cost — and where you arrive is not yet fixed; you shape it by arriving, which means you cannot know what you are stepping into, only that your step will help make it. There is no far-step home from the edge; you walk back.

tree.name: The Edge of the Map
tree.grants: Step beyond the known world into the unmapped, helping call a new place into being by arriving.
tree.cannot: It costs nearly all you have, the destination is unfixed until you make it, and there is no quick way back — the edge of the map is reached by stepping and left by walking.

rankDeltas.delta: SPECIAL: STEP BEYOND THE KNOWN WORLD into the unmapped, HELPING CALL A NEW PLACE INTO BEING BY ARRIVING. The capstone is a KIND (travel that CREATES destination) at near-total cost.

intensity.conserve: REFUSED — you cannot half-step off the edge of the map; you are on it or past it.
intensity.surge: REFUSED — it already costs nearly all you have.

bounds.text: it costs your whole remaining energy pool and leaves you at zero, unable to use any craft until you rest a full night
THE DESTINATION IS UNFIXED UNTIL YOU ARRIVE

abilities.plainly: A travel action that moves you or someone else. Its strength is rated 9 out of 10 across a scope of 4. Range is 9999 Limit: iT Costs Nearly All You Have.

abilities.name: The Held Hour
abilities.narrationHints: You take the hour and HOLD it — not stopping time, but holding one hour of it open, refusing to let it pass until what needs doing in it is done.
abilities.description: The Hourkeeper art of the held hour — keeping a single hour open past its natural passing, a pocket of kept time in which the necessary can be finished. The timekeepers' patient gift.
abilities.notFor: It holds time, it does not reverse it — a held hour ends and cannot be held twice over the same ground. And holding an hour costs you the holding of it; you do not rest inside kept time, you carry it.

tree.name: The Held Hour
tree.grants: Hold a single hour open past its passing, keeping time for what must be finished.
tree.cannot: It cannot rewind, only delay the passing; the same hour cannot be re-held; and the one holding time does not get to rest in it.

tree.name: The Kept Hours
tree.grants: Hold more than a single hour — a night's work finished inside a kept evening, a siege's preparation inside one afternoon. And those working within it now benefit fully: what they finish in kept time is genuinely finished.
tree.cannot: The holder still does not rest, and holding several hours ages the holder for real. The same ground cannot be re-held. And an hour kept too long is noticed — the Hourkeepers hold that time collects its debts, and the GM decides when.

rankDeltas.delta: hold MORE THAN A SINGLE HOUR — a night's work finished inside a kept evening, a siege's preparation inside one afternoon

intensity.conserve: hold part of it — half the kept time, and the cost is light
intensity.surge: double it; THE HOLDER STILL DOES NOT REST, and holding several hours ages you through all of them

bounds.text: IT CANNOT REWIND, ONLY DELAY THE PASSING
THE SAME HOUR CANNOT BE HELD TWICE
THE HOLDER STILL DOES NOT REST — holding several hours ages you through all of them

abilities.plainly: A defend action that makes or animates something. Its strength is rated 7 out of 10 across a scope of 2, and lasts for about an hour Ranks: rank 2 extends scope. Limit: iT Cannot Rewind, Only Delay The Passing.

abilities.name: The Long Foreseeing
abilities.narrationHints: You follow one thread of what-will-be all the way down — not a glimpse but the whole long braid of consequence, every branch, to where it finally comes to rest.
abilities.description: The Hourkeeper capstone — the long foreseeing, one possible future traced to its very end rather than glimpsed. To see this far is to carry a certainty most are mercifully spared, and to be bound to what you have seen.
abilities.notFor: One thread, once, at enormous cost — and what you see, you are bound by; a foreseeing this deep changes how you act, and acting changes the future you saw. You cannot un-know the end you followed to.

tree.name: The Long Foreseeing
tree.grants: Trace one possible future to its very end, seeing the whole braid of its consequence.
tree.cannot: It costs nearly all you have, it binds you to what you've seen, and the deepest mercy of not-knowing is one you have chosen to give up.

rankDeltas.delta: SPECIAL: TRACE ONE POSSIBLE FUTURE TO ITS VERY END, seeing THE WHOLE BRAID OF ITS CONSEQUENCE. The capstone is a KIND (complete consequence-sight) at near-total cost — AND IT BINDS YOU TO WHAT YOU HAVE SEEN.

intensity.conserve: REFUSED — a half-traced future is a guess, and the Hourkeepers do not dignify guesses.
intensity.surge: REFUSED — it already costs nearly all you have.
